faqs.question: What is the Carousel 12 Plus Reaction Station used for?
faqs.answer: It's a patented 12-position station that simultaneously heats, stirs, and refluxes samples under an inert atmosphere, used for parallel reaction screening and solid supported reagent synthesis.

faqs.question: Do you offer a demo of the Carousel 12 Plus?
faqs.answer: Yes, Inkarp can arrange a demonstration on your own application.

faqs.question: How can I work with smaller volumes in my Carousel 12 Plus?
faqs.answer: Use reduced-volume tubes, which bring the reaction volume down to 1 to 5 mL, compared to the standard 5 to 20 mL tubes.

faqs.question: How do I purge my tubes for an inert atmosphere?
faqs.answer: Connect the central gas inlet via flexible tubing to a two-way stopcock, then alternate between vacuum and inert gas to quickly clear unwanted air from all 12 tubes.

faqs.question: How do I set up sub-ambient cooling for my reactions?
faqs.answer: Add the optional HDPE cooling reservoir, which brings the achievable temperature down to -78°C; the base configuration alone doesn't reach sub-ambient temperatures.

faqs.question: Does every tube really stir at the same speed?
faqs.answer: Yes. The patented design positions every tube and its stir bar equidistant from the hotplate's central magnet specifically to keep stirring speed identical across all 12 positions.

faqs.question: What tubing do I need for the reflux/inerting head?
faqs.answer: This is confirmed directly by Inkarp based on your specific installation.

faqs.question: How accurate is the temperature control?
faqs.answer: ±1°C, using the hotplate's digital control or an optional Pt1000 sensor for block or solution temperature.

faqs.question: Can I add reagents without breaking the inert atmosphere?
faqs.answer: Yes, through the replaceable Suba-Seal septum in each Easy-On cap, using a syringe.

longForm.heroLead: 12 tubes, stirred at exactly the same speed. Patented, not left to chance. Run 12 reactions on one stirring hotplate and it's easy for stirring speed to drift between positions, some tubes closer to the magnet than others. Carousel 12 Plus doesn't let that happen. Every tube and its stir bar sit equidistant from the hotplate's central magnet, patented specifically to keep stirring identical across all 12 positions, from 100 to 1,400 rpm. Heating reaches 180°C sustained, 220°C briefly, held to ±1°C, with the option to control block or solution temperature directly. Reflux runs through a water-cooled head that removes with the tubes still attached, and the whole system operates under a genuine inert atmosphere: individual gas-tight caps, a radial distribution system, and a two-way stopcock to purge each tube in seconds.

sections.eyebrow: Uniform Heating, Stirring and Reflux Across 12 Positions
sections.title: Uniform Heating, Stirring and Reflux Across 12 Positions
body: Twelve independent reactions running identically depends on three things behaving the same way across every position, not just one.

Stirring is uniform because of geometry: every tube and its stir bar sit equidistant from the hotplate's central magnet, which is the actual mechanism, not a side effect of the circular layout. Heating and cooling are uniform because the reaction tubes themselves are precision engineered from heavy-walled borosilicate glass specifically to maximise and equalize heat transfer. Reflux stays uniform because the water-cooled head creates the same cooling zone in the upper part of every tube simultaneously.

sections.title: Cooling Mechanism and Stirrer Protection
body: Reaching -78°C with a physical cooling mixture solves the temperature problem. Keeping the stirrer running at that temperature is a separate problem, and this reservoir solves both.

The HDPE reservoir accepts dry ice/acetone and other freezing mixtures directly, giving manual control across the full ambient to -78°C range rather than relying on electronic cooling. The insulated foam core is what actually protects the stirrer mechanism from that cold, while also holding the temperature steady over long reaction times and cutting down the condensation and ice that would otherwise build up on outer surfaces and tube walls.

faqs.question: What is the Carousel Work-Up Station used for?
faqs.answer: It's a 12-position parallel work-up station used for filtration, phase separation, liquid/liquid extraction, and SPE, reducing post-synthesis processing bottlenecks.

faqs.question: Why is vacuum-free design an advantage here?
faqs.answer: It removes taps, valves, and drip needles from the process entirely, which simplifies cleaning, cuts consumable costs, and specifically prevents columns from drying out the way a vacuum manifold can.

faqs.question: How do I speed up a work-up beyond gravity flow?
faqs.answer: Add the SpeediFlow Booster, a hand-held pressuriser that individually controls flow through a specific column, with a safety relief valve venting at 6 to 8 psi.

faqs.question: How do I set up a sequential, multi-step work-up?
faqs.answer: Add the optional third rack, stacked above the standard two-rack configuration, for staged processing.

faqs.question: How do I add a second rack to the station?
faqs.answer: Pull out the spring-loaded knob and rotate it 90 degrees to lock the second rack into place.

faqs.question: What column chemistries are available?
faqs.answer: 20 µm filtration, phase separation, silica, SCX, aminopropyl, and SAX acetate, all in the standard 70 mL format.

faqs.question: Can I use non-standard column sizes with SpeediFlow?
faqs.answer: Yes, using the optional SpeediFlow adapters, which cover 15, 25, 70, and 150 mL columns, plus the Whatman AutoCup.

faqs.question: Does this station work with my existing Carousel Reaction Tubes?
faqs.answer: Yes, the same Carousel Reaction Tubes used in Carousel 12 Plus and Cooled Carousel 12 Plus fit the lower collection rack directly.

faqs.question: Is the SpeediFlow Booster safe from over-pressurisation?
faqs.answer: Yes, it includes a safety relief valve that vents automatically at 6 to 8 psi.

faqs.question: What is the price of the Carousel Work-Up Station in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on your rack configuration and column chemistry needs. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your work-up technique is confirmed.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of the Carousel Work-Up Station in India?

longForm.heroLead: No vacuum, no valves, no drip needles. Twelve columns, still under precise control. Post-synthesis work-up usually means a vacuum manifold, a set of valves, and columns that dry out the moment the vacuum pulls too hard. This station skips all of that. Twelve columns run in parallel, gravity-fed by default, with no taps or drip needles to clean or replace. When you need more speed than gravity gives you, the hand-held SpeediFlow Booster pressurises each column individually, with a safety relief valve venting at 6 to 8 psi so pressure never gets away from you. Two identical racks lock together, and a third stacks on top when the work-up needs a second step. The same Carousel Reaction Tubes from your Carousel 12 Plus system slot straight into the collection rack underneath.

sections.title: Carousel Work-Up Station at a Glance
sections.description: Everything you need to configure this station: why vacuum-free design actually matters, how gravity and SpeediFlow flow control differ, which column chemistry fits your work-up, and Inkarp installation and service support.
sections.subheading: No vacuum, no valves, no drip needles. Twelve columns, still under precise control.
body: Vacuum-free isn't just simpler, it prevents a real failure mode. Columns that would dry out under a vacuum manifold don't, because there's no vacuum pulling on them.
Gravity is the default, and it's genuinely enough for most work. SpeediFlow exists for when you specifically need more speed, not as a required accessory.
SpeediFlow's pressure is engineered, not just applied. A Viton O-ring, trigger-locked, with a safety relief valve venting at 6 to 8 psi so over-pressure isn't a risk you have to manage manually.
Rack stacking is a real mechanism, not a stated feature. A spring-loaded knob and a 90° rotation is the actual locking action between racks.
Sequential work-up is a genuine three-tier capability. An optional third rack stacks above the second for multi-step processing.

This isn't a closed system. The same Carousel Reaction Tubes from Carousel 12 Plus work here, and SpeediFlow's adapters extend to standard columns and the Whatman AutoCup beyond this station entirely.
Six real column chemistries are already confirmed. Filtration, phase separation, silica, SCX, aminopropyl, and SAX acetate, not a generic "columns available" claim.

sections.title: Vacuum-Free Design and Flow Control
body: Removing the vacuum manifold from a work-up station changes more than the assembly process.

Without taps, valves, or drip needles, there's simply less to clean, replace, or leak, and columns don't dry out from vacuum pulling too hard, a genuine, common problem with conventional manifolds. Gravity handles most work-ups on its own. When speed matters more, the SpeediFlow Booster pressurises a single column at a time, through a mechanically expandable Viton O-ring locked by its trigger, with a safety relief valve venting automatically at 6 to 8 psi so over-pressurizing a column isn't something you have to actively avoid.
